title: Ledger Nano X from MediaMarkt Trier, shared by @coinjoined

purchase.dateNote: Inferred: @coinjoined posted a photo of the store that morning as "mystery shopping", named the city as Trier, and posted the opened implant the same afternoon. The posts don't say outright that this device came from that visit.

components: Printed antenna inside the case, marked AC-A2205-NX 欧亚版-V1.1, with a coax lead to a u.FL connector
Black implant board next to the Nano X board, carrying a large module and a QFN chip
Replacement battery: MB 281544, 3.7 V 130 mAh 0.481 Wh, dated 2026-04-03
Small board on the battery, partly legible marking …X-1350-D
Twisted enamelled wires from the battery board to the Nano X board, next to the USB-C connector
implant.notes: The post shows three photos of an implanted Nano X and one of a genuine Nano X for comparison. That morning, @coinjoined had posted a photo of a MediaMarkt store in Trier, Germany, as "mystery shopping", so the device was most likely bought there. The replacement battery has the same label and date as the first MediaMarkt device. The antenna is the same part number, AC-A2205, as that device's antenna (AC-A2205-NANO-X-欧亚版-V1.0), but a later revision, V1.1. The post lists the allegedly affected resellers so far as MediaMarkt and Saturn in Germany, Cryptobilis in Malaysia, Ozon in Russia, and Singapore airport.

sources.text:
There shouldn't be any cables. First 3 images show the implant, last image a genuine @Ledger Nano X.
Allegedly affected resellers so far: MediaMarkt, Saturn 🇩🇪, Cryptobilis 🇲🇾, Ozon 🇷🇺 and Singapore Airport 🇸🇬

images.caption: Opened case: a black implant board with a large module and a u.FL antenna connector sits beside the green Nano X board.
The Nano X board lifted out, with the replacement 130 mAh battery (2026-04-03) wired on. The coax lead runs to a printed antenna in the case, marked AC-A2205-NX 欧亚版-V1.1.
Close-up: twisted enamelled wires run from the small board on the battery to pads on the Nano X board, next to the USB-C connector.
For comparison, the post's last photo: a genuine Nano X, with no extra wires or boards and its original 100 mAh battery.
The MediaMarkt store in Trier, posted that morning as "mystery shopping".
